text:
alejandra: noticing a slow mem growth on a few long streaming sessions this morning, ~200MB over 3h on a single replica. not OOM but uphill trend. anyone else seeing this?

nguyen: saw the alert. looks correlated with tool-loop-heavy workloads (repeated tool calls inside stream). session_count steady, but heap goes up.

leo: can you paste a heap profile or pprof snapshot? want to check retained-by graphs.

alejandra: pasted the pprof diff to the artifacts bucket: gs://redwood-ci/pprof/5071234567/pprof.diff.txt. quick snippet from top nodes: 
```
pprof: cumulative bytes
--- retained ---
kv_page_entry: +154M
session_object: +40M
pointer_table: +22M
```
Seems a lot held by kv_page_entry.

maya: interesting — earlier regressions were about sticky page refs during streaming, but this looks like accumulation of small anchors rather than single big pages. any evidence of refcounts not dropping?

nguyen: instrumented refcount ops on a staging run. counts increment when tool calls write into KV (prefix writes) but occasionally decrement path not taken if an error path returns early. see logs: 
```
2026-03-15T08:12:01Z store.put prefix=tools/exec/123 -> refcount +1
2026-03-15T08:12:01Z store.put prefix=tools/exec/123 -> refcount +1
2026-03-15T08:12:01Z store.put failed write -> early return (no refcount rollback)
```
That would leave anchors alive.

leo: that matches sampling trace we took: held-by shows caller chain from toolchain write -> anchor_register -> session_keepalive. If error path misses anchor_release, ref stays.

alejandra: repro steps I used: run streaming chat with nested tools that create short-lived in-memory pages, then induce a synthetic write failure (disk full on replica) and continue normal traffic. memory grows. without induced failures, growth is minimal.

maya: so two hypotheses: 1) error path missing release, 2) concurrent GC/race where anchor is unlinked but refcount not visible due to a missed CAS. which is more likely?

nguyen: initial traces point to the missing-release case. I added a quick assert in staging: ensure every successful put has a matching anchor_release in same request context. saw ~0.4% of requests missing release after we re-enabled a legacy error branch.

leo: can we hotfix by adding a defer-style release in the higher-level code? low-risk?

alejandra: added a patch to guard early returns in PR #5421 (small). ran 12h staging run with induced failures: memory plateaued and didn't climb. patch seems promising.

maya: nice. any perf cost from extra releases? negligible (microbench showed <0.5% p99 token latency change).

nguyen: a second follow-up: we also saw increased fragmentation — many small page objects created and retained. even after releases, fragmentation keeps RSS up until compaction runs. compaction interval is 1h currently. shorter compaction helps at the cost of CPU.

leo: what's the compaction tradeoff? did you run a config sweep?

nguyen: ran two runs: compaction=15m reduced steady RSS by ~120MB but added ~8% CPU on the worker. compaction=5m got RSS back to baseline but CPU +25% and slight p99 latency bump.

maya: maybe we can add adaptive compaction: trigger on per-replica fragmentation signal (fragmentation_ratio > 0.6) rather than fixed interval. should only run when necessary.

alejandra: agree. filed an RFC ticket INF-1218 to propose adaptive compaction + a nonblocking background sweep. linking plan in the ticket.

leo: next steps: 1) merge PR #5421 (release guard) 2) add a small metrics gauge for "pending_anchors" 3) implement adaptive compaction PoC in a feature branch 4) roll to canary with error-injection enabled for a week.

maya: also add a lightweight sampling profiler in prod that captures held-by stacks for top-5 kv_page_entry owners when pending_anchors spikes. that'll help catch other missing-release spots.

alejandra: created follow-up tasks and assigned owners in the ticket. I'll merge the patch after one more reviewer. thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy triggered: canary/kvrun/patch-5421 -> 3/3 replicas. monitor group: eng-runtime.

leo: I'll keep an eye on the canary dashboards (kv.pending_anchors, kv.fragmentation_ratio, worker.rss). ping if any anomaly.

nguyen: logging the measurement we care about for postmortem: after patch + adaptive compaction PoC, target is <50MB growth over 12h under our tool-heavy trace.

maya: timeline: merge this week, PoC next week, canary + error injection 1 week.

alejandra: thanks team. closing the loop here; will update INF-1218 with canary results.
